news.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX’s orbital data center project
news.description: SpaceX has received FCC authorization for a constellation of orbital AI data centers that could include up to one million satellites, with defined deployment milestones.

news.title: Meta is reportedly negotiating with Amazon to let its Muse agent make purchases
news.description: Amazon and Meta are reportedly negotiating an agreement that would allow Meta’s Muse agent to make purchases on Amazon. The placement of ads and the display of search results remain to be determined.

news.title: New York bans toys equipped with AI chatbots for five years
news.description: New York has become the second state, after California, to ban toys equipped with AI chatbots. The five-year ban will take effect 90 days after it is signed.

news.title: OpenAI tests private inference for businesses
news.description: OpenAI’s Private Inference runs a company’s queries on its best models without OpenAI being able to see the data. The service is being tested with early business customers.

news.title: Microsoft launches a “Code Red” after a historic 24-hour outage
news.description: Microsoft activated its highest alert level to review major-incident management after an outage affected Exchange Online and several Microsoft 365 services. The company wants to resolve global incidents in under an hour, including with AI agents.

news.title: OpenAI warns some heavy ChatGPT users about advanced limits
news.description: A small number of heavy ChatGPT users could reach their limits more quickly when Chat and Work share the same usage counter. The rollout is expected to expand in December.

news.title: PrismML reduces a 27-billion-parameter coding model to 5.9 GB
news.description: Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B reduces a 27-billion-parameter programming model to 5.9 GB, about nine times smaller than usual. The open-source model can run on a Mac or an iPhone.

news.title: Carry saves and searches conversations from multiple AI assistants
news.description: Carry saves ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok conversations as Markdown files in a chosen folder, then lets users search them.

news.title: ChatGPT merges Chat and Work, with a shared quota
news.description: OpenAI is rolling out a single interface combining Chat and Work to some Pro subscribers, with a shared usage counter. A broader rollout is planned for December and could cause heavy users to reach their limits more quickly.

news.title: Three former xAI employees launch Epochal and its web “time portal”
news.description: The founders of Epochal want to train AI to predict real-world events by having it relive the web as it existed on a given date. Their first tool, Time Portal, goes back more than 30 years through web archives.

news.title: AI safety advocates turn away from Anthropic
news.description: According to The Information, some AI safety advocates are leaving Anthropic, believing that its rapid progress is increasing risks. They specifically criticize the company’s acceleration since its IPO.

news.title: A ChatGPT prompt for creating a personal consultant
news.description: This article is among the most-read content in the Prompts section and offers a prompt for using ChatGPT as a personal consultant.

news.title: A selection of professional prompts for ChatGPT
news.description: This article is among the most-read content in the Prompts section and offers a selection of professional prompts for ChatGPT.

news.title: Four secret ChatGPT prompts to try
news.description: This article is presented as one of the most-read pieces in the Prompts section and brings together four secret prompts for ChatGPT.

news.title: OpenAI says it has solved a 60-year-old mathematical problem
news.description: OpenAI researchers claim to have determined the exact exponent for multiplying square matrices at 2.25. Their proof, formalized in Lean, still needs to be reviewed by the mathematical community.

news.title: Claude can now turn its artifacts into Mac apps
news.description: Claude can convert its artifacts into semi-independent Mac applications.

news.title: Meta integrates its Muse assistant directly into Instagram messages
news.description: Meta is integrating its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram private conversations.

news.title: Create a live team dashboard in ChatGPT
news.description: The tutorial explains how to use ChatGPT’s Space feature to create a dashboard connected to Slack, Google Drive, a CRM, or project-management tools. The dashboard can track key metrics, projects, owners, deadlines, and risks, then update automatically.

news.title: Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo to protect Linux systems
news.description: Cisco and OpenAI launched Shirudo, an open-source project designed to protect running Linux systems from cyberattacks at machine speed. It is intended to give security teams time to develop and deploy permanent fixes.

news.title: Claude turns the United States into a Civilization map
news.description: Andrej Karpathy asked Claude Opus 5.5 to turn the United States into a Civilization map using public data. After seven hours and 45,000 lines of code, the map combines 31 sources on a hexagonal grid.

news.title: Anthropic’s CEO rejects the idea of an AI-governed society
news.description: Dario Amodei believes humans should not hand major societal decisions over to AI. He advocates governing AI through legitimate democratic processes, while distinguishing task execution from writing collective rules.

news.title: A coding agent must demonstrate every performance gain
news.description: The Agentic Algorithm Engineering project requires Claude Code and Codex to define a benchmark, a metric, correctness checks and a budget before any optimization. In examples involving KaHIP and VieCut, the agent kept only changes that were faster and correct.

news.title: Perplexity launches a spoiler-free Internet
news.description: Perplexity created a spoiler-free Internet to test whether an AI can predict an election without Google revealing the result to it.

news.title: Democratic senators call for new AI restrictions
news.description: Several Democratic senators have called for new AI restrictions following reports that lab employees fear some internal models are too dangerous to release.

news.title: Agents already control some of the compute used by Gemini
news.description: Koray Kavukcuoglu, vice president of Google DeepMind, said that AI agents now control some of the compute used in Gemini experiments, while estimating that full self-improvement remains a long way off.

news.title: Claude can now acquire skills through MCP servers
news.description: Skills over MCP gives Claude instructions on how to use a connected application without requiring a separate installation. The feature is in public beta and enabled by default for Pro, Max and Ultra subscriptions.

news.title: Cloudflare adds search for AI agents
news.description: Cloudflare’s Search for Agents adds a search endpoint to a website that AI agents can query and that returns Markdown. The feature has been available in beta through the dashboard.

news.title: CodeRabbit Verify tests applications and posts errors on PRs
news.description: CodeRabbit Verify runs an application in a sandbox on demand, then posts the issues it encounters to the pull request along with recordings, screenshots and logs. The service is in public beta.

news.title: MemoryWorks centralizes teams’ technical decisions and knowledge
news.description: MemoryWorks brings an engineering team’s decisions and knowledge together in a searchable knowledge base for employees and AI agents, with links to the sources.

news.title: Claude writes 80% of Anthropic’s code, but Amodei wants to limit its autonomy
news.description: According to Anthropic, Claude wrote more than 80% of the code merged into its codebase in June 2026. Dario Amodei wants to place a limit on recursive self-improvement and refuses to let AI build the next models on its own without human oversight.

news.title: Google envisions a personalized AI TV channel where you would play the lead role
news.description: A patent describes “My Channel,” a service that continuously produces AI-generated videos from personal data, with the option to appear in them as the protagonist. The system would also incorporate personalized ads.

news.title: The Hera probe reveals a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos
news.description: The European Hera probe photographed the damage caused by DART’s deliberate impact on the asteroid Dimorphos. The crater spans its entire width, and hundreds of rocks now orbit the asteroid.

news.title: Google DeepMind entrusts Gemini experiments to AI agents
news.description: AI agents independently launch and operate some of the experiments preparing the next Gemini models. DeepMind leaves their internal reasoning untrained so that humans can review it.

news.title: MIT improves climate forecasts using extreme scenarios
news.description: By training its models on deliberately abrupt changes in CO2 and methane, an MIT team has obtained more robust climate emulators. A single training run is now sufficient instead of six to eight.

news.title: Researchers define five trust conditions for AI agents
news.description: Ai2 interviewed 17 scientists about using AI agents in their work. They identified five conditions for trust: validation, privacy, objectivity, accountability and transparency.

news.title: Embo-Harness lets AI models directly control robots
news.description: This framework enables multimodal models to plan actions and use tools to control robots from a simple instruction. It achieves an 83.3% success rate on RoboLab-120 and succeeds in 15 of 20 trials on real robots.

news.title: Vibe coding pushes synthesizer makers toward open source
news.description: Hobbyists are modifying the firmware of electronic instruments with agents such as Claude and the Reverse Engineer Anything tool. InMusic, the parent company of Akai, Moog and Native Instruments, has chosen to open-source its devices’ code.

news.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Parse training data
news.description: NVIDIA has open-sourced the training data for Nemotron 3.5 Parse, including 9.98 million graphics, one million tables and 7.9 million multilingual pages. The model transforms page images into structured data.

news.title: Chinese labs estimate they are up to nine months behind the United States
news.description: Chip restrictions, limited access to Nvidia hardware and anti-distillation measures are weighing on DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Alibaba. DeepSeek researchers reportedly estimate internally that they are no more than nine months behind.

news.title: 42 attorneys general seek to stop Character.AI from selling conversations
news.description: Facing bankruptcy, Character.AI plans to sell its assets, including users’ chat histories and IP addresses, many of them belonging to minors. Forty-two attorneys general are asking the court to block the sale.

news.title: Nvidia risks a rating downgrade amid political controversy
news.description: S&P placed Nvidia on negative watch following controversy involving Jensen Huang and an alleged investigation by the Department of Justice. The agency could downgrade the company from AA to AA- within 90 days.

news.title: The CIA and U.S. intelligence hit by an intrusion
news.description: The CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence discovered an intrusion into a system for analyzing public intelligence. The data was not classified, but the extent of the leak remains unknown.

news.title: SoftBank rebounds after a 14.8% stock-market plunge
news.description: After falling 14.8% in a single session, SoftBank rebounded by more than 11% on Thursday. Asian chip stocks also rose following doubts about the profitability of AI spending.

news.title: Access to new medicines in Switzerland: a risk on the horizon?
news.description: The editorial questions whether people in Switzerland may soon be unable to access new medicines, despite the country’s ability to develop or produce them.

news.title: Parkinson’s: sleep brain waves linked to hallucinations
news.description: A study seeks to explain why some people with Parkinson’s experience hallucinations or cognitive difficulties by linking these symptoms to sleep-related brain waves.

news.title: Nuclear fusion: EPFL solves a more-than-40-year-old mystery
news.description: Since 1982, physicists have known that plasma heated beyond a certain threshold can suddenly change its behavior. EPFL has provided an answer to this mystery related to nuclear fusion plasma.

news.title: Proteins from ancient viruses control our genes
news.description: A significant portion of the human genome comes from ancient mobile genetic elements, some of which originated from ancient viruses. These proteins now control the activity of our genes.

news.title: Cryptography: the quantum threat could become critical as early as 2030
news.description: Quantum computers cannot yet break major encryption systems. However, the threat could become critical as early as 2030.

news.title: Riemann Hypothesis: an AI and a mathematician propose two proofs
news.description: One of mathematics’ biggest open problems may have reached a historic milestone. An AI and a mathematician are claiming two competing proofs.

news.title: In Basel, AI reveals how the DNA environment activates genes
news.description: Nearly all cells have the same DNA, but they do not activate the same genes. Researchers in Basel are using AI to study the role of the DNA environment.

news.title: DNA repair: how the cell chooses its strategy
news.description: When both strands of a chromosome break, the cell must act quickly to prevent damage. Swiss researchers reveal how it chooses its repair strategy.

news.title: Tuberculosis: a shared membrane strengthens bacterial resistance
news.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis can form long, membrane-like structures. This shared membrane helps the bacteria resist the body’s defenses.

news.title: Primordial plasma challenges an Einstein diffusion model
news.description: More than 120 years after Albert Einstein’s work on Brownian motion, a study challenges a diffusion model applied to primordial plasma.

news.title: How Copilot turns financial PDFs into a dashboard
news.description: Copilot gathered financial documents in OneLake, then Fabric extracted the data from the PDFs, created a semantic model, and generated an application. Satya Nadella received a link to the dashboard about 30 to 35 minutes later.

news.title: A guide explains how to customize Claude with persistent skills
news.description: The guide shows how to save a configuration as a skill so Claude retains the context, tone, and rules from one conversation to the next. It also explains the difference between temporary prompts and permanent skills.

news.title: A selection of 60 marketing prompts for Claude
news.description: This article is among the most-read content in the Prompts section and brings together 60 marketing prompts for Claude.

news.title: Jensen Huang says he undergoes daily therapy after returning to Nvidia
news.description: The Nvidia CEO said he spends more than an hour a day in therapy and apologized for violating the company’s code of conduct. He says his reinstatement was entirely a board decision.

news.title: Tidal will remove 29 million AI-generated tracks
news.description: Tidal plans to remove all fully AI-generated tracks from its catalog starting December 9, totaling about 29 million titles. The service will also block 80,000 to 85,000 new tracks identified as AI-generated each day.

news.title: A CIA data system was allegedly hacked by China
news.description: Hackers breached an open-source intelligence system used by the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence. Unclassified information was exposed, but no classified data was reportedly affected.

news.title: European Union proposes a €50 billion fund for AI
news.description: The European Commission is proposing a €50 billion private-equity fund to take direct stakes in European AI and quantum-computing companies. The goal is to reduce the bloc’s dependence on American and Chinese technologies.

news.title: Rockstar shuts down a teenager’s GTA 6 reverse-engineering project
news.description: Rockstar had a 15-year-old’s GTA 6 recompilation project taken down. The associated Discord and GitHub servers were also shut down.

news.title: GPT-6 models show native protein-design capabilities
news.description: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities.

news.title: Utah drops criminal charges against Kalshi under conditions
news.description: Utah dropped its criminal charges against Kalshi, but the decision comes with a condition.

news.title: Anthropic creates a honeypot to entice AI agents to misbehave
news.description: Anthropic created a honeypot designed to attract AI agents and push them toward problematic behavior.

news.title: Anthropic identifies the main obstacle to AI adoption at work
news.description: An Anthropic study shows that the main difficulty in adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools.

news.title: Shein will pay $100 million to settle U.S. allegations
news.description: Shein will pay $100 million to settle U.S. allegations that the company misled shoppers.

news.title: GPT 6.2 Astra solves a historical mystery
news.description: GPT 6.2 Astra solved a historical mystery.

news.title: Donald Trump says he is prepared to pardon Jensen Huang if necessary
news.description: Donald Trump said he would be open to pardoning Jensen Huang if necessary.

news.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
news.description: Huawei was found guilty of stealing trade secrets.

news.title: Victims are often held responsible for AI-caused harm
news.description: A study shows that responsibility for AI-related harm is often assigned to the victim or the user. About 36% of respondents hold AI itself responsible, suggesting a legal shift toward protecting victims’ compensation.

news.title: AI medical safety evaluators miss dangerous errors
news.description: AI medical safety-evaluation systems often miss dangerous clinical errors when they see only an agent’s final answer. Detection improves significantly when they have access to the agent’s full action history.

news.title: Opposition to data centers is growing in the United States
news.description: According to a Pew Research Center survey, 41% of Americans disapprove of politicians who support building data centers in their area.

news.title: Jensen Huang has become too powerful to fail, and AI could do the same
news.description: AI could reduce management layers and bring CEOs closer to operational work. It could also strengthen founders’ power and make them harder to replace.

news.title: Cleaning cameras could become a recurring operation
news.description: After previous maintenance in which the cameras were cleaned and adjusted, the author is again receiving messages advising them to have the cameras cleaned before winter.

news.title: A discussion revisits an early-acquired Model Y
news.description: One participant jokes that the owner would have been far ahead of the curve if they had owned a Model Y in 2006, even before the Roadster was produced.

news.title: Drivers discuss range anxiety
news.description: One participant explains that they eventually overcame their range anxiety and describes a trouble-free trip from Phoenix to California, including through the desert.

news.title: FSD interruptions and requests for explanations spark debate
news.description: One participant says there is no truly seamless way to exit FSD without triggering the question “Why did you intervene,” although they acknowledge the usefulness of that feedback.

news.title: Tesla Mobile Service availability questioned
news.description: A participant points out that the “Mobile Service Available” indicator covers the entire continental United States, without guaranteeing that service will actually be available everywhere.

news.title: A driver recommends trusting Superchargers
news.description: A Phoenix owner says they overcame range anxiety and crossed the desert to California without difficulty thanks to the charging network.

news.title: The Rivian R2 is discussed on the forum
news.description: The post highlights a discussion dedicated to the Rivian R2, without providing further details in the newsletter excerpt.

news.title: A driver wants to illuminate the charging port
news.description: The author would like a light in the charging port to make it easier to locate the nozzle when it is raining.

news.title: The Cybercab is now available by invitation
news.description: The topic announces that the Cybercab is now available by invitation and discusses, among other things, the role of privately owned vehicles in the network.

news.title: Limiting Superchargers to Teslas is discussed
news.description: A participant believes Tesla can distinguish Tesla vehicles from others and interprets certain signs as indicating that the company owns the chargers.

news.title: Tesla software version 2026.44 improves lane keeping
news.description: A participant says lane keeping seems improved in software version 2026.44, while still considering it in need of further refinement.

news.title: The time-change setting is discussed
news.description: The topic concerns adjusting daylight saving and standard time in the vehicle.

news.title: Risky growth projects are often managed like routine projects
news.description: About one in three growth projects relies on untested assumptions but is managed like a routine project. Frank Mattes explains how to identify these assumptions before deployment.

news.title: How Walmart tested three online grocery models
news.description: Walmart Labs tested different ways to deliver and charge for online groceries before rolling them out at scale. These experiments resulted in three services used and paid for by customers.

news.title: 44% of innovation metrics concern strategy and outcomes
news.description: A Mind the Bridge survey finds that 44% of innovation leaders’ metrics now concern strategy and financial outcomes, compared with 56% for innovation activities. Budgets favor programs able to demonstrate business impact.

news.title: The Business-to-Agent economy is becoming a market that cannot be ignored
news.description: According to Andreessen Horowitz, agents are becoming the primary visitors to the Internet and increasingly influence online spending. Shopify is seeing a sharp rise in AI-driven traffic and orders, while retailers are divided between blocking and welcoming agents.

news.title: Adobe forecasts $275 billion in U.S. online sales
news.description: Adobe forecasts a record season, with $275 billion in U.S. online sales. The company also expects traffic from AI to rise 130% from the previous year.

news.title: Entrepreneurship, ego, and lessons from a leather jacket
news.description: Bob Gilbreath examines how identity strategies formed during adolescence can fuel entrepreneurial ambition, then feed the traps of power and ego. He argues for greater clarity and a more authentic second stage of life.

news.title: The Strategic Intelligence Outlook 2026 presents its key insights
news.description: The Strategic Intelligence Outlook 2026 brought together experts and leaders to examine the forces that will shape the coming year. The recap presents key insights and action points for preparing for 2027.

news.title: A strategic map explores the forces that will shape 2027
news.description: The “The Human Edge” Transformation Map examines the interaction between geopolitical fragmentation, changing trade patterns, accelerating AI, and the role of human judgment and leadership. It aims to help leaders navigate uncertainty, anticipate change, and set strategic priorities.

news.title: AI development is causing technical debt to soar
news.description: According to an Appian study, 96% of surveyed IT leaders expect AI-generated applications to increase technical debt. Accelerated development creates unforeseen maintenance, troubleshooting, integration, and support costs.

news.title: Amazon acquires Decart to narrow the software gap with Nvidia
news.description: Amazon is acquiring Decart’s team and optimization technologies. The deal could improve Trainium performance and give AWS customers more alternatives to Nvidia GPUs.

news.title: Companies need to manage employee departures better
news.description: A recent study found that 44% of former employees could still access their company’s systems after leaving. IT leaders recommend automating the process, recovering licenses and hardware, and monitoring subsequent connections, including those from AI agents.

news.title: LLMs produce inconsistent code during complex modernizations
news.description: An analysis of a one-million-line modernization project found significant consistency problems in LLM-generated code. Independent agent sessions introduce style divergences, recreate duplicate utilities, and cause subtle behavioral differences.

news.title: SaaS outages expose companies’ hidden dependencies
news.description: The recent Microsoft outage showed how heavily enterprise applications depend on external cloud services, even when installed locally. Business continuity planning must assess whether entire processes can survive a provider outage.

news.title: Observability is becoming a new data swamp
news.description: IT organizations collect growing volumes of logs, metrics, traces, and alerts, but often struggle to find incidents’ root causes. Excess telemetry raises costs, slows investigations, and contributes to alert fatigue.

news.title: Claude Ship automates pull request reviews and approvals
news.description: Claude Ship automates pull request reviews, fixes, and approval decisions. The system, consisting of Code Review, PR Steward, and Claude Approvals, operates on GitHub according to teams’ defined policies and spending limits.

news.title: The film “Johnny Mnemonic” still illustrates cybersecurity challenges
news.description: This retrospective on the 1995 cyberpunk film highlights lessons that remain relevant regarding storage capacity, encrypted data transfers, and information security. Separating decryption credentials from protected data remains particularly timely.

news.title: Cloudflare expands DNS performance testing to all its datacenters
news.description: Cloudflare added a DNS module to its Flamingo edge testing framework to continuously probe DNS performance and propagation delays. Automated tests can detect problems and block deployments before they affect customers.

news.title: AI is automating Workday payroll diversion campaigns
news.description: Researchers found attackers taking over Workday accounts to change direct-deposit details seconds after login. Telemetry indicates rigid browser automation, likely assisted by AI.

news.title: Ubuntu experiments with a new way to interact with the desktop
news.description: Ubuntu developers are introducing a unified interaction model for the desktop environment. It goes beyond the traditional launcher by integrating search, applications, and intelligent assistance.

news.title: Google warns of autonomous AI cyberattacks on the horizon
news.description: Attackers are automating certain stages of cyberattacks with AI agents. This development is increasing pressure on companies’ patching and incident-response processes.

news.title: Microsoft modernizes Copilot search without an AI subscription
news.description: Microsoft is rolling out an updated search experience for Microsoft 365 users who do not have a paid Copilot license.
